blocks.x: Anthony Gordon has sided with Thomas Tuchel’s assertion that controlling games through possession is not part of English football’s DNA. Although Gordon revealed surprise at being substituted when England were 1-0 up in their World Cup semi-final against Argentina, the winger refused to blame the defeat on Tuchel’s decisions and argued that wider cultural issues influenced the side’s collapse.

England’s perennial struggle to keep the ball when under pressure flared when a place in the final was within touching distance in July, allowing Argentina to fight back and go through with two late goals. The pain has not gone away and there has been intense scrutiny of Tuchel’s role in Atlanta. The head coach’s tactical choices were criticised and he faced a backlash after saying “ball possession” was not in his team’s DNA.

But Gordon, who thinks he will always be scarred by losing against Argentina, sided with Tuchel’s observations about England’s style as he looked towards the Nations League game against Spain on Saturday. The 25-year-old admitted the side had an ingrained inability to control games but argued they should stop trying to copy other nations.
Gordon has gained an insight into the Spanish understanding of how to use the ball since his move to Barcelona. His view is that England should lean more into their physical strengths.

“Culturally it’s not just that tournament or that game where we couldn’t control a game,” Gordon said. “As a nation we don’t have that strength like the Spanish, where we control games like they do. It’s not in us. I’m not sure it’s something that can be taught. Playing in Spain I can speak with an educated view on the way they keep the ball.

“It’s much different than I’ve ever experienced in this country, so I’m not sure we can ever get that. We can definitely get better – or maybe go the other way and really play to our strengths, which is play physical, play direct football and on the counterattack.”

I look at some of the decisions they take on the ball sometimes and think: ‘I’m not sure how you’ve seen that.’”

Gordon opened the scoring against Argentina and was surprised to be replaced by Ezri Konsa when Tuchel made the first of two defensive moves and switched to a back five after the hydration break in the second half.

blocks.c: Thomas Tuchel talks to his England players

blocks.x: “I’d just scored,” Gordon said. “I’m really good when I play off adrenaline. When I score, I normally don’t have many bad games, because I get into an untouchable mode of confidence.

“But as a winger I come off most games. It’s normal, it’s usually the position that’s targeted first for substitutions, because the player on the bench in your position is usually quick, and usually really good.”

Gordon defended Tuchel and said England’s performances did not match their level in training. “It makes a lot of sense to me why the manager would then go more safe and more defensive [against Argentina],” he said.

“As players we could have done more to take the initiative, to control the game. We had the best team, we had the best players in that semi-final, and in the last 20 minutes we didn’t play the best football. That’s something the manager can’t really affect.”
Gordon said his Barça teammates had told him England would have given Spain a tougher game than Argentina in the final. Spain dominated in New Jersey, winning 1-0 in extra time.
